result.title: Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning for Multi-Objective Alignment
result.summary: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with several objectives, such as helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty, typically relies on preference judgment for each objective, growing the annotation cost linearly with the number of objectives. Active preference learning can reduce this cost by selecting the comparisons whose labels are expected to change the policy most. Existing remedies either lack an objective-aware query selection mechanism for the multi-objective setting or regard conflicting preferences as harmful, therefore excluding them from the training data. We introduce OGC-DPO (Objective-conditioned Gradient Coverage DPO), an active learning framework that treats each (response pair, objective) combination as a separate query and measures its informativeness through the policy's own implicit gradient, without relying on an external reward model. OGC-DPO then selects the queries that most expand each objective's gradient coverage. Empirical experiments across varying numbers of objectives demonstrate the effectiveness of OGC-DPO over existing active preference learning methods under the same annotation cost. Further analysis demonstrates that informative conflicts, rather than being uniformly harmful, provide a useful policy training signal.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 OGC-DPO，在多目标对齐中把每个「响应对—目标」组合视为独立查询，用策略自身的隐式梯度估算信息量并优先选择能扩大各目标梯度覆盖度的样本，以降低偏好标注成本，并指出冲突偏好也能提供有用训练信号。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按目标分组的梯度覆盖式选样与「冲突样本也有监督价值」的观察，可能可供核查用于多目标 latent 推理训练数据的筛选与监督分配；但论文不涉及视觉输入或推理期状态，联系仅停留在方法层面。
